subject: english
question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

He often **changes plans** while doing his work. So, his tasks remain incomplete.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Change horses in midstream**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Change horses in midstream"** means to change plans or leaders during an activity or process that is already underway, which can lead to complications or failure. (मध्य में योजना बदलना)

 
 
• **Example: **It's not wise to change horses in midstream; we should stick to our current plan until the project is completed.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, it is said that while working, the person frequently modifies his plans. Thus, his tasks are still unfinished.** **

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Change horses in midstream**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **In seventh heaven** (सातवें आसमान पर): Refers to being extremely happy or joyful.

 
 
• **Example:** He was in seventh heaven when he won the lottery.
 
 
 
• **Break a leg** (शुभकामनाएँ देना): A phrase used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance.
 
 
• **Example: **Before the audition, his friends told him to break a leg.
 
 
 
• **Spill the beans** (राज़ खोल देना): To reveal secret information inadvertently or prematurely.
 
 
• **Example:** She accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
